title: Protect the interior and clean the surrounding trim
text: Leave the surrounding plastics in place, as shown in this installation. Wipe dust from the trim before bringing exposed film into the car, including the low edge behind the rear seats. Protect the interior from application water and keep dirty shoes and tools off it.
quality: Clean glass is only half the job. Dust sitting on nearby trim can reach the adhesive as the film passes behind it.
alt: Installer wiping the plastic trim beneath the Porsche Targa rear window

title: Scrub the entire inside surface of the rear glass
text: Work over the whole pane with a scrubber suitable for the glass. The installer repeats the cleaning rather than relying on one quick pass. He specifically warns against using a razor on this rear window because of the defroster system.
quality: Pay as much attention to the corners and bottom edge as the easy-to-reach center. One missed speck can stay visible under the finished tint.
alt: Scrubber working across the inside of the Targa rear glass

title: Change your squeegee angle around the curves
text: Squeegee the cleaning solution away in overlapping passes. At the curved sides, turn the tool sideways so its edge stays against the glass. Use a suitable reaching tool along the bottom edge, then wipe the plastics again.
quality: If half the squeegee lifts off the glass, it is leaving water and contamination behind. Change the angle instead of repeating the same ineffective stroke.
alt: Squeegee angled across the curved side of the Targa rear window

title: Wet the adhesive as you separate the liner
text: The film in this video has already been cut and heat-shaped to the rear window. With it supported on a glass work surface, separate the liner while spraying the exposed adhesive. Keep spraying as you work across it, then lay it back down wet.
quality: Keep the adhesive from drying out or touching dusty trim. The shaped film wants to curl, so support it rather than letting it fold onto itself.
alt: Installer separating the liner from shaped tint film on a glass work surface

title: Make a tight, even back roll
text: Smooth the larger air pockets while the film is supported on the glass, then roll the film and liner into a compact roll. Keep the first turns tight and continue evenly across the pane. This is the back-roll, or California-roll, method shown in the video.
quality: A loose start makes the rest of the roll harder to control. An even roll is easier to carry into the cramped rear cabin without creasing the film.
alt: Hands forming an even roll of tint film on the vertical glass work surface

title: Unroll inside without letting the film catch
text: Wet the inside glass and the tight upper corners before opening the roll. Support the film on your arm, peel the liner away gradually and keep adding slip solution as you unroll. Let the film move on the wet glass instead of dragging it into place dry.
quality: Stop and reposition if the film catches. A sharp fold can leave a crease; forcing the roll through a tight corner makes that more likely.
alt: Tint film being unrolled and supported inside the Targa rear window

title: Check the fit before anchoring the film
text: Spread the film evenly across the glass and ease out areas with too much tension. Check the perimeter for light gaps while the film is still movable. In the video, a second person checks from outside, and the installer uses a bright object to help judge coverage.
quality: Do not lock down the center until the edges line up. A small positioning adjustment now is easier than trying to move film after squeezing out the water.
alt: Installer checking the positioned film against the edge of the Targa rear glass

title: Anchor the middle, then work outward
text: Hold the film steady and make the initial squeegee passes in the middle to create an anchor. Work from that center toward each side, following the curve. Revisit sections while they are still wet rather than leaving water behind to dry.
quality: Move the water and tension toward the nearest edge. Dragging film from one side of the window to the other can create new wrinkles. The installer also warns that working a drying section can leave visible marks.
alt: Squeegee working outward from the anchored middle of the rear-window film

title: Work trapped water out of the lower corners
text: Look for narrow raised pockets, often called fingers, that return after a pass. Check whether the tool is reaching the bottom of the pocket. Change direction or use an appropriate firmer or reaching tool, as the installer does, so the water has a path out.
quality: A finger that keeps coming back may still hold water. Flattening its top without clearing the bottom can leave a dry air pocket later.
alt: Installer using a firm squeegee to work water out near the curved edge

title: Set the remaining fingers and inspect the edges
text: The final sequence uses controlled heat and a tool to settle the remaining fingers, with the heat directed away from the trim. Use the film maker’s guidance for heat and application; the demonstration’s timing is not a universal setting. Recheck the lower edge, corners and visible glass before calling the installation finished.
quality: Look for lifting edges, returning fingers, light gaps and trapped contamination. Do not assume more heat will fix a crease or a speck. Inspect the finish as well as whether the film stays down.
alt: Heat gun aimed toward the rear glass during the final edge-finishing sequence
